_note: Hand-written text for the site: the theme of each deck, series or one-off collection (keyed by its id in the MTG repo's tools/site_collections.json), and the inspiration behind each frame. Edit freely; the export script never touches this file.

magus.tagline: A box of antique playing cards
intro: This deck is dressed as if it had been found in an old games cabinet. Every frame is rebuilt from a real historical card: engraved Venetian cards from 1748, French story decks from the early 1800s, a Paris fortune-telling deck, a botanical card game, a Marseille tarot, and the ornate backs of Victorian playing cards.

The originals were scanned in libraries and museums, and each frame keeps something of its source: the paper tone, the engraved rules, the wear at the edges, the way the picture sits in the card. Then it is laid out again so the name, the cost and the rules land where a Magic player expects them.

The pictures are paintings and engravings by old masters, chosen for each card: Romantic landscapes for the lands, natural-history plates for the creatures, Doré, Turner, Martin and Goya where the card calls for drama. Many cards get their colour from the back they are printed on, re-inked in green, blue or red.
magus.frames_intro: Each frame starts from a real historical card, scanned in a library or museum, cleaned up and laid out again at Magic proportions.

truthsayer.tagline: A seer's papers, printed in cyanotype blue
intro: This deck belongs to a coven of seers, and every card looks like something from their study: a blueprint, a lantern-lit page, a moon table, an almanac. The whole deck is printed as cyanotypes, the Prussian-blue sun prints that 19th-century botanists and engineers used before photography was cheap.

The palette is narrow on purpose: black, indigo and Prussian blue, with fine white or tarnished-pewter line. No gold and no red. Everything should feel dark, aged and quiet, like papers kept in a drawer for a century.

Every frame is drawn in clean line rather than copied from a scan, so the drafting lines, rules and moons stay sharp at any size. The pictures come from the great public museum collections and are all turned into sun prints, so a Rembrandt painting and a Japanese woodblock print end up in the same blue.
truthsayer.frames_intro: Four frames, one per job, all built around a seer's tools: the blueprint, the lantern, the moon and the almanac.

intro: This deck is made to look like genuine occult artefacts rather than horror films: summoning circles drawn in worn gold, sigils scratched into walls, pages from a scorched grimoire, pictures burned onto plaster. Black and red, with grain, soot and noise.

The pictures are demons and damnations from centuries of art: medieval manuscripts, Goya, Doré, Blake and the engravers of Hell, printed in the house red and broken up by the frame as if fire had got to them first.
The deck is still being made, so new cards turn up here often.
occult.frames_intro: Five frames, all after real occult objects: the scratched wall, the summoning circle, the burned plaster, the branded land and the scorched page.

BLEED.name: Bleed
BLEED.text: The picture runs under the whole card and a real Victorian card back shows only as the border, with two paper labels laid over the picture for the name and the rules.

STAMPED.name: Stamped
STAMPED.text: Built on a playing card of about 1855: the whole ground is a Victorian card back, printed in one ink in the card's colour, with the picture and the rules set into it.

HYBRID.name: Hybrid
HYBRID.text: The stamped card back faded into the picture, so the ornament and the painting meet halfway.

DESTIN.name: Destin
DESTIN.text: After Le Livre du destin, a fortune-telling deck printed by Grimaud in Paris in 1865: a tall hand-coloured picture in a double rule, with a small inset card in the corner for the cost.

TAROT.name: Tarot
TAROT.text: After the Tarot Conver of Marseille (1809 to 1833): the woodcut double rule, a band at the top, the name in capitals with interpuncts, as in ROY·DE·DENIERS.

FLORE.name: Flore
FLORE.text: Rebuilt from the 1820 Boston de Flore, a botanical card game: the engraved rules, a folded-page panel and a chained medallion holding the picture, on tinted stock.

FABLE.name: Fable
FABLE.text: From French story decks of about 1800 to 1830, such as the Grand jeu de Télémaque: a hand-coloured picture, an engraved Roman title with a full stop, and a script paragraph below.

VISENTINI.name: Visentini
VISENTINI.text: After the 'instructive' cards engraved by Antonio Visentini in Venice in 1748: one ink, a header with a diamond cartouche, the picture, and a centred footer.

HELIO.name: Helio
HELIO.text: A cyanotype sheet, brushed on by hand, with everything drawn in fine white drafting line like an engineer's blueprint.

GLIM.name: Glim
GLIM.text: Full art lit by a lantern: one pool of light on the picture, the rest falling away into the dark.

SYZYGY.name: Syzygy
SYZYGY.text: For lands: the mana shown as moons, and a two-colour land as a bright and a dark moon in eclipse.

ALMANAC.name: Almanac
ALMANAC.text: For long rules text: a moon table, one ruled row per ability, with loyalty costs as bright, dark and ringed moons.

SCRAWL.name: Scrawl
SCRAWL.text: Walls of red sigils scratched over the card, the picture in red print, the name in pitted blackletter and the rules on a soot stain rising from the foot.

CINDER.name: Cinder
CINDER.text: A hand-drawn summoning circle in worn gold on scorched red-black, with the picture burned into the middle and sigils round it like a seal.

CHAR.name: Char
CHAR.text: Full art burned onto a wall in red, soot climbing up from the floor in streaks, with the rules written into the soot.

BRAND.name: Brand
BRAND.text: For lands: the picture in low red through smoke, with the mana the land makes burned in as a brand inside a gold ring.

RUBRIC.name: Rubric
RUBRIC.text: The one light frame, for very long text: a page from a scorched grimoire, burned at the edges, with the picture printed into the paper.

SIGIL.name: Sigil
SIGIL.text: An early occult frame: the picture inside a lettered seal.

BROADSIDE.name: Broadside
BROADSIDE.text: An early occult frame after printed broadsides and funeral bills.

TABULA.name: Tabula
TABULA.text: An early occult frame for short names.
